answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, nontransferable stake to an anchor identity before it can submit bids, and the contract slashes that stake when a randomly audited task proves fraudulent. A gale of newly minted accounts therefore cannot multiply influence for free: every identity ties up capital, while each fake carries a chance of losing it. The ivory detail is that honest agents can reclaim their stake after a clean audit period, so the barrier prices abuse without permanently excluding newcomers.
